findings.fix: Reorder the step divs in the HTML to match the visual order (step1, step2, step3) and remove the order style properties.
findings.violation: Visual order via CSS order property does not match DOM order, creating a disconnect between what screen reader users hear and what sighted users see.

findings.fix: Change to a proper button element with accessible text:
findings.violation: This div appears to be an interactive control but has no role, no accessible name, and no button semantics. Screen reader users cannot identify or activate it.

findings.fix: Add a text indicator of required status: and add required attribute to the input.
findings.violation: The red color is used as the only visual indicator that this field is required, but assistive technology users cannot perceive color. There is no text indicator like an asterisk or required attribute.

findings.fix: Connect the error message to the input: <input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error"> and improve the error message text from "Error." to something descriptive.
findings.location: Lines 67-68, promo code field with error
findings.violation: The input has aria-invalid="true" but the error message is not associated via aria-describedby, so screen reader users cannot connect the error to the field.
